text:
sam: quick note — the 'Usage by tier' example in metering/analytics doc is showing 0.00 values in the table when you run the cURL snippet.

lina: ugh, thanks for catching. do you have the request you ran? which header set did you use?

sam: used the example in https://redwood.dev/docs/metering/snippets — curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Project: demo" ... response tokens show costs but the docs table has different numbers.

mike: sounds like mismatch between pricing tier lookup and the example query. docs panels use billing_rate_v2 now; older snippets use billing_rate.

sam: here's the snippet I ran:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Metering-Tier: pro" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?start=2026-02-01&end=2026-02-28"
```

lina: ok that's the issue — docs snippet still sets X-Metering-Tier instead of the new X-Rate-Tier header. small find-and-replace will fix. i'll open a PR.

jen: also add a short migration note in the pricing/tiers page about header rename and query name change (billing_rate -> billing_rate_v2) so customers don't get confused.

product-analytics: fyi we've rolled billing_rate_v2 to prod 2026-02-15; old queries still work but the example numbers differ because v2 applies a discount tier calc.

lina: created PR #6421 with two commits: update SDK snippet, update dashboard query example, and add migration note. preview link: https://deploy-preview.redwood.dev/6421

docs-ci-bot: link check failed — /docs/metering/old-snippet redirects 302 -> 404. leaving a note on the PR.

lina: pushed a followup commit to fix the redirect path and added a unit test for the snippet rendering.

mike: can someone sanity-check the numbers? i ran the new snippet and got totals matching the dashboard after using X-Rate-Tier: pro.

sam: confirmed, numbers align now. :tada:

jen: merge when green. add changelog blurb under docs/metering: "Updated metering examples for header and billing_rate_v2; clarified pricing tier calc."

docs-ci-bot: tests passed. PR merged by lina at 2026-03-15 15:12 UTC.

sam: thanks everyone. added a quick note in the SDK migration checklist for the header rename so this doesn't regress. :thumbsup:
